headline: Last good window to direct-sow fast fall greens — get spinach, lettuce, arugula, radishes, and kale in now for an October harvest.

tasks.title: Direct-sow fall greens
tasks.detail: With ~8-9 weeks to first frost (mid-Oct), sow quick 40-60 day crops now: spinach, lettuce, arugula, radishes, kale, cilantro, and Asian greens. Water the seedbed daily until they germinate in the late-summer heat.

tasks.title: Keep picking summer crops
tasks.detail: Tomatoes, zucchini, cucumbers, beans, and peppers are peaking. Harvest every day or two — picking regularly keeps plants producing and stops zucchini from turning to baseball bats.

tasks.title: Late blight & powdery mildew
tasks.detail: Humid coastal air makes this prime time for late blight on tomatoes (brown greasy spots, fast spread) and white powdery mildew on squash and cucumbers. Remove affected leaves, improve airflow, and never compost blighted foliage.

tasks.title: Water deep and steady
tasks.detail: Give beds about 1 inch per week, watering at the base in the morning. Consistent moisture prevents tomato cracking and blossom-end rot during the August heat.

tasks.title: Open up tomato plants
tasks.detail: Strip the lower 12 inches of leaves off tomatoes and thin dense growth to boost airflow and sunlight to ripening fruit. Stop topping/feeding heavily so plants ripen what they've set before frost.

tasks.title: Order garlic for October
tasks.detail: Buy seed garlic now while supply is good — you'll plant cloves in mid-to-late October, a few weeks before the ground freezes, for a bigger harvest next summer.
